raw:
{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulate grid-cell/column-level total runoff (surface + subsurface) generation for a column representative of the American River (near Nile, WA) headwater area in the Naches basin using single-column ELM.",
      "Produce a time series of column-integrated runoff (QRUNOFF, QOVER, QDRAI) and snow/soil moisture states driving that runoff at daily resolution."
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "A true daily STREAMFLOW hydrograph at the American River USGS gauge — this requires channel/river routing (e.g., MOSART) over the contributing watershed, which a single-column configuration cannot provide.",
      "A basin-integrated NSE against the observed gauge hydrograph — single-column runoff is per-unit-area and not spatially aggregated or routed, so a defensible NSE against gauge discharge is not computable without routing and full watershed coverage.",
      "Timing/attenuation effects of channel travel time and floodplain storage that shape the observed hydrograph."
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 1,
  "n_justification": "Single-column ELM represents one point/land-unit; the American River headwater in the Naches basin is approximated by one representative montane forest column. Additional columns would not create routed streamflow, so a single diagnostic column is used to characterize runoff generation.",
  "columns": [
    {
      "id": "american_river_naches_headwater",
      "lat": 46.98,
      "lon": -121.18,
      "soil_texture": "gravelly sandy loam (glacial/andesitic mountain soil)"
    }
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "2000",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2019",
    "STOP_N": "20",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2000-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER",
      "QDRAI",
      "QOVER_LAG",
      "QSNOMELT",
      "SNOWDP",
      "H2OSNO",
      "SNOW",
      "RAIN",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "H2OSOI",
      "ZWT",
      "TSA",
      "TSOI",
      "FSNO",
      "QINFL"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "River/runoff routing model (MOSART) to convert land runoff into channel streamflow at the gauge — NOT available in single-column mode",
    "Full spatial (distributed) watershed configuration covering the American River contributing area",
    "USGS observed daily discharge for American River near Nile, WA (e.g., USGS 12488500) for NSE evaluation",
    "Basin delineation and area-weighting to aggregate distributed runoff before routing"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Column coordinates place a representative montane conifer forest point in the American River headwaters of the Naches River basin, WA.",
    "GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing (2000-2019) is used as the meteorological driver; site-specific gauge-adjacent forcing would improve realism.",
    "Runoff is reported per-unit-area and cannot be equated to gauge discharge without routing.",
    "A meaningful NSE against the observed streamflow hydrograph is deferred pending a MOSART-coupled, spatially distributed run; single-column output alone cannot yield it.",
    "A multi-year spin-up (recycling forcing) precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack states."
  ]
}

answerable: Simulate grid-cell/column-level total runoff (surface + subsurface) generation for a column representative of the American River (near Nile, WA) headwater area in the Naches basin using single-column ELM.
Produce a time series of column-integrated runoff (QRUNOFF, QOVER, QDRAI) and snow/soil moisture states driving that runoff at daily resolution.
not_answerable: A true daily STREAMFLOW hydrograph at the American River USGS gauge — this requires channel/river routing (e.g., MOSART) over the contributing watershed, which a single-column configuration cannot provide.

A basin-integrated NSE against the observed gauge hydrograph — single-column runoff is per-unit-area and not spatially aggregated or routed, so a defensible NSE against gauge discharge is not computable without routing and full watershed coverage.
Timing/attenuation effects of channel travel time and floodplain storage that shape the observed hydrograph.

parsed.n_justification: Single-column ELM represents one point/land-unit; the American River headwater in the Naches basin is approximated by one representative montane forest column. Additional columns would not create routed streamflow, so a single diagnostic column is used to characterize runoff generation.
requires_capabilities: River/runoff routing model (MOSART) to convert land runoff into channel streamflow at the gauge — NOT available in single-column mode
Full spatial (distributed) watershed configuration covering the American River contributing area
USGS observed daily discharge for American River near Nile, WA (e.g., USGS 12488500) for NSE evaluation
Basin delineation and area-weighting to aggregate distributed runoff before routing
assumptions: Column coordinates place a representative montane conifer forest point in the American River headwaters of the Naches River basin, WA.
GSWP3/CLMNCEP atmospheric forcing (2000-2019) is used as the meteorological driver; site-specific gauge-adjacent forcing would improve realism.
Runoff is reported per-unit-area and cannot be equated to gauge discharge without routing.
A meaningful NSE against the observed streamflow hydrograph is deferred pending a MOSART-coupled, spatially distributed run; single-column output alone cannot yield it.
A multi-year spin-up (recycling forcing) precedes the analysis period to equilibrate soil moisture and snowpack states.
